basis: Cash basis, continuing operations. Comparator: FY21 (year ended 30 June 2021) vs FY20 (year ended 30 June 2020). The FY21 Profit Announcement KPI table states 'Net interest margin (%) 2. 03 [FY21] 2. 07 [FY20] (4)bpts' under 'Group Performance from continuing operations'. The FY20 Profit Announcement independently reports the same continuing-operations FY20 figure (2.07%, vs 2.09% in FY19), so this comparator is not an artefact of the FY21 restatement. On an including-discontinued-operations basis, the movement is -5bps (2.08% to 2.03%) -- see disagreements.

drivers.name: Higher liquid assets
drivers.narrative: Non-lending interest earning assets (mostly liquids) rose $20bn (12%) to $195bn, funded by strong deposit growth. These assets yield far less than loans (0.38% vs 3.25% average yield in FY21), so a bigger low-yielding pool dilutes the Group margin even though CBA states the dollar impact on net interest income was small.

citations.quote: Liquid assets: Decreased margin by 4 basis points driven by increased lower yielding non-lending interest earning assets, including liquid assets.
a $17 billion increase in average liquid asset balances mainly due to strong customer deposit growth
Higher Liquids ... (4) ... Minimal impact on NII

drivers.name: Asset pricing
drivers.narrative: Business lending margin fell 1bp from COVID-19 support repricing, and consumer finance margin fell 1bp as the share of interest-earning credit card balances declined. Home lending was net flat: repricing added 9bps but was offset by customers switching from variable to fixed-rate loans (-5bps) and price competition/discounting (-4bps).

citations.quote: Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 2 basis points driven by lower business lending margins (down 1 basis point) from repricing actions to support businesses during COVID-19, and lower consumer finance margins (down 1 basis point)

Home lending margins were flat, reflecting repricing (up 9 basis points), offset by the impact of customers switching from higher margin loans to lower margin loans, particularly from variable rate to fixed rate loans (down 5 basis points) and increased competition (down 4 basis points).
Bus. Lending (1) ... Consumer Fin. (1) ... Home loans: Pricing +9 Switching (5) Discounting (4)

drivers.name: Deposit pricing and funding costs
drivers.narrative: Earnings on transaction and savings deposits fell as the RBA cash rate was cut (net -7bps in the Profit Announcement's wording; the presentation splits this into the cash rate cut, -8bps, partly offset by investment-deposit repricing, +1bp). This was partly offset by a higher benefit from the replicating portfolio (+2bps) and lower wholesale funding costs (+2bps). Average deposit cost fell from 1.30% to 0.61% and the $18.6bn Term Funding Facility drawdown cost only 0.23%, consistent with a cheaper funding base.

citations.quote: Funding costs: Decreased margin by 3 basis points, reflecting lower earnings on transaction and savings deposits mainly due to decreases in the cash rate (down 7 basis points), partly offset by higher benefits from the replicating portfolio (up 2 basis points) and lower wholesale funding costs (up 2 basis points).
Impact of cash rate cut (8) ... Investment +1 ... R. Portfolio +2 ... Wholesale +2

drivers.name: Portfolio mix
drivers.narrative: The average deposit funding ratio rose from 71% to 77% as transaction and savings deposits grew strongly, customers switched to at-call deposits, and the TFF was drawn down (+4bps). This was partly offset by an unfavourable asset-mix effect (-2bps) from the decline in higher-margin consumer finance balances.

citations.quote: Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by a higher average deposit funding ratio (30 June 2021: 77%; 30 June 2020: 71%) due to strong growth in transaction and savings deposits, customers switching to at-call deposits, and the drawdown of the TFF (up 4 basis points), partly offset by an unfavourable impact from asset mix (down 2 basis points)
Higher deposit funding ratio and at-call deposit balances, drawdown of the TFF +4 ... Decline in higher margin consumer fin. balances (2)

drivers.name: Basis risk (including replicating portfolio)
drivers.narrative: Basis risk is the spread between 3-month BBSW and the 3-month OIS rate. That average spread narrowed during FY21, lifting the margin, even though CBA says it structurally reduced its exposure to basis risk through growth in cash-rate-linked deposits and the shift to fixed-rate home loans.

citations.quote: The Bank's margin increased 3 basis points reflecting a decrease in the average spread notwithstanding a structural reduction in exposure to basis risk due to strong growth in cash rate linked deposits and a mix shift towards fixed rate home loans.

drivers.name: Capital and other
drivers.narrative: Lower earnings on Group capital as rates fell cut margin by 3bps (the equity hedge rolls onto lower rates over time), partly offset by a higher New Zealand contribution (+1bp) from lower wholesale funding costs and favourable mix, partly offset by RBNZ cash rate cuts.

citations.quote: Capital and other: Decreased margin by 2 basis points driven by lower earnings on Group capital due to the falling interest rate environment (down 3 basis points), partly offset by increased contribution from New Zealand (up 1 basis point), reflecting lower wholesale funding costs and favourable portfolio mix, partly offset by the impact from RBNZ cash rate cuts.

drivers.name: Treasury and Markets
drivers.narrative: Higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets lifted the margin by 2bps.

citations.quote: Treasury and Markets: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets.

disagreements.topic: Size of the movement depends on which reporting basis is used
values: -4bps, continuing operations (2.07% to 2.03%) -- CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 22
-5bps, including discontinued operations (2.08% to 2.03%) -- CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 22
disagreements.reason: Both the Results Presentation's driver walk (PDF page 63) and the Profit Announcement's driver narrative (PDF pages 32-33) are explicitly footnoted 'Presented on a continuing operations basis'. The continuing-operations block is also listed first in the KPI table, and it is the only basis for which a driver walk exists.

disagreements.topic: Granularity of the funding-cost driver differs slightly between the two documents
values: Profit Announcement (PDF page 32): 'decreases in the cash rate (down 7 basis points)' as a single net figure
Results Presentation (PDF page 63): 'Impact of cash rate cut (8) ... Investment +1' shown as two separate bars
disagreements.preferred: Both, read together -- the presentation's split reconciles exactly to the Profit Announcement's net figure
disagreements.reason: -8 + 1 = -7, matching the Profit Announcement's net wording. This is a presentation-granularity difference, not a numerical conflict; the -3bps total for the driver is identical in both documents.

disagreements.topic: The Results Presentation also shows a simplified 3-bucket view of the same movement
values: Detailed 7-driver walk (PDF page 63, 'Full year'): liquids -4, asset pricing -2, funding -3, mix +2, basis risk +3, capital & other -2, treasury & markets +2
Simplified re-aggregation (PDF page 29, 'This Year'): higher liquids -4, impact of lower rates -6, management actions/other +6
disagreements.reason: Both sum to -4bps and are internally consistent (the simplified view's 'impact of lower rates' and 'management actions/other' net to zero, matching the six non-liquids drivers in the detailed walk, which also net to zero: -2-3+2+3-2+2=0). The detailed walk carries full narrative support in the Profit Announcement text; the simplified view is a highlights-slide summary of the same numbers.

limitations: All seven driver contributions are CBA's own internal margin-analysis decomposition, disclosed identically (in bps) in both the Profit Announcement narrative (PDF pages 32-33) and the Results Presentation waterfall chart (PDF page 63). The documents do not disclose the underlying model, so the split cannot be independently recomputed from raw balance and rate data.
The driver walk is presented on a cash, continuing-operations basis only. Neither document publishes a statutory-basis NIM driver walk.

Sub-driver figures inside each bar (e.g. home loan pricing +9bps, switching -5bps, discounting -4bps) were read from a bar chart (Results Presentation, PDF page 63) using the chart's positioned text labels rather than a data table; they are precise to the nearest whole basis point as printed.

The FY20 comparator (207bps, continuing operations) is identical between the FY20 Profit Announcement (as originally reported for FY20 vs FY19) and the FY21 Profit Announcement (as the restated FY21 comparator), so the FY20-to-FY21 restatement noted in both documents does not affect this movement.
Quantified drivers sum exactly to the stated movement (-4bps), so the residual is 0; this reflects that CBA's own walk is constructed to reconcile, not an independent check of its accuracy.
